plan: With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, i.e., shade by 1/3. This balances the trade-off between probability of winning and profit margin. My value is $26, so optimal bid ≈ 26 × (2/3) = $17.3. This maximizes expected profit given rational competitors following similar strategies.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for n=3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $31, so I'll bid approximately $20.7 to maximize expected profit while still having a reasonable chance to win against the other two bidders' likely bids.

With three bidders and values uniformly distributed on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to bid a fraction (n-1)/n = 2/3 of my value, assuming others bid similarly rationally. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $24, so I'll bid approximately $16, which should give a good expected profit while maintaining a reasonable chance of winning.
